items.stem: Why should a safety system moderate model outputs and not only user inputs?

options.text: A safe-looking prompt can still produce unsafe output, so outputs must be checked too
options.rationale: Correct: harm can appear in the generation even when the input seems benign.

options.text: Inputs are never a source of risk
options.rationale: Inputs are also risky; both sides need controls.

options.text: Output moderation makes the model faster
options.rationale: It adds a check; it is about safety, not speed.

options.text: Outputs are always safe by default
options.rationale: Outputs can be unsafe, which is why they are moderated.

items.explanation: Correct: harm can appear in the generation even when the input seems benign.

items.stem: Which TWO are real trade-offs when tightening content guardrails? (Select TWO.)

options.text: More aggressive blocking increases false-positive refusals of safe requests
options.rationale: Correct: stricter rules refuse more legitimate requests.

options.text: Overly strict guardrails can reduce the assistant's usefulness
options.rationale: Correct: safety and usefulness must be balanced.

options.text: Tighter guardrails always eliminate every bypass
options.rationale: No guardrail is perfect; bypasses still occur.

options.text: Blocking more content lowers the token cost of answers
options.rationale: Blocking is a safety measure, not a cost optimisation.

items.explanation: Correct: stricter rules refuse more legitimate requests.

items.stem: What practice best keeps guardrails effective as new bypass attempts appear?

options.text: Ongoing red-teaming and monitoring to find and fix gaps
options.rationale: Correct: continuous testing and monitoring catch new bypasses.

options.text: Freezing the guardrails permanently after launch
options.rationale: Static guardrails fall behind new attacks.

options.text: Removing output moderation to save compute
options.rationale: That weakens safety rather than maintaining it.

options.text: Trusting that attackers will stop trying
options.rationale: Adversaries keep adapting; guardrails must too.

items.explanation: Correct: continuous testing and monitoring catch new bypasses.
